Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
suppliers below. For a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of pure dimension
$n$ with a chosen ample line class $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, its rational
cohomology is finite-dimensional pure Hodge in each degree, functorial for
pullback along holomorphic maps of the analytifications. Cup product has Hodge
type $(0,0)$ and $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$. For $0\le k\le n$ the
hard-Lefschetz maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are rational isomorphisms,
and for $k>n$ so are the complementary maps $\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$; the rational
primitive summands satisfy the Hodge–Riemann positivity of
[[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], and
the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization. Rational
Hodge substructures split orthogonally. The same absolute positivity and
hard-Lefschetz statements hold for real Kähler classes, and primitive kernels
vary continuously along Kähler families. Rational splittings and isomorphisms
persist after extension to any characteristic-zero field. This package does
not supply weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular
intersection-cohomology purity, or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.

Let $N$ be a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space $H$ over a field $F$ ([[def-nilpotent-endomorphism]]). An **admissible filtration** is an increasing finite filtration $W$ of $H$ by linear subspaces ([[def-linear-subspace]]): $W_i\subseteq W_{i+1}$ for all $i$, $W_i=0$ for all sufficiently negative $i$, $W_i=H$ for all sufficiently positive $i$, such that

$$N(W_i)\subseteq W_{i-2}\quad\text{for all }i,\qquad N^r:\operatorname{Gr}^W_r\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-r}\text{ is an isomorphism for every }r\ge0,$$

where $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i:=W_i/W_{i-1}$ and the second map is the one induced by $N^r$, which is well defined because $N^r(W_r)\subseteq W_{-r}$ and $N^r(W_{r-1})\subseteq W_{-r-1}$. There is a unique admissible filtration $W$, and it is given intrinsically by

$$W_i=\sum_{a,b\ge0,\ a-b=i}\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b .$$

If in addition $S$ is a nondegenerate bilinear form on $H$ with $S(Nv,w)+S(v,Nw)=0$ for all $v,w$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]], [[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]), and $U^\perp:=\{x\in H:S(u,x)=0\text{ for every }u\in U\}$ for a subspace $U$, then $(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$ for every $i$, and consequently $S$ induces a perfect pairing between $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}$; moreover for $i\ge0$ the form $S_i([v],[w]):=S(v,N^iw)$ on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i$ is well defined and nondegenerate.

derivations.claim: Put $d=b_n-b_{n-2}$. By [F1] each map $L+\epsilon\eta:H^n\to H^{n+2}$ has kernel of dimension $d$, and these kernels are Hodge subspaces by [F1]. The matrix of the map is polynomial in $\epsilon$; choose a maximal minor that is nonzero on a sufficiently small punctured interval $(0,\epsilon_0)$. On that interval row elimination expresses a basis of the kernel $\Lambda_\epsilon$ by rational functions of $\epsilon$; wedge the $d$ basis vectors, clear denominators, and divide by the lowest power of $\epsilon$ occurring. The result is a nonzero polynomial exterior vector whose value at $\epsilon=0$ defines a point $\Lambda$ of the Grassmannian $\mathrm G(d,H^n)$, and $\Lambda=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\Lambda_\epsilon$: the Plücker coordinates of $\Lambda_\epsilon$ are given by that rational exterior vector, so they converge to the value at $0$. A different maximal minor gives the same punctured family of planes and hence the same limit point. Stability of a plane under a fixed endomorphism of $H^n$ is a closed condition on the Grassmannian, so $\Lambda$ is stable under every Hodge projector, being a limit of the Hodge subspaces $\Lambda_\epsilon$; hence $\Lambda$ is a real Hodge subspace. If $u_\epsilon\in\Lambda_\epsilon$ and $u_\epsilon\to u$, then $Lu_\epsilon=-\epsilon\eta u_\epsilon\to0$ by continuity, so $Lu=0$ and $\Lambda\subseteq D$.

Put $E_j:=\eta^j\ker(L^j:H^{n-2j}\to H^n)$, so $M=E_1$. We prove by induction on $i$ that
$$M\cap E_1^\perp\cap\cdots\cap E_i^\perp=M\cap W_{-i}H^n .$$
For $i=0$ both sides equal $M$, because $\ker L\subseteq W_0$ by [F2] and $\eta$ preserves $W$ by (a), so $M\subseteq W_0$.

Induction hypothesis: fix $i\ge0$ and assume the displayed equality $M\cap E_1^\perp\cap\cdots\cap E_i^\perp=M\cap W_{-i}H^n$; we must derive the equality for $i+1$. Since $\ker L^{i+1}\subseteq W_i$ by [F2] and $\eta$ preserves $W$, one has $E_{i+1}\subseteq W_i$; condition (c) (with $a=-i-1$, $b=i$ and $a+b=-1<0$) therefore makes $M\cap W_{-i-1}H^n$ orthogonal to $E_{i+1}$, and so $M\cap W_{-i-1}H^n\subseteq M\cap E_1^\perp\cap\cdots\cap E_i^\perp\cap E_{i+1}^\perp$ by the induction hypothesis. This is one inclusion of the equality for $i+1$.

For the converse inclusion let $\alpha=\eta\lambda\in M\cap W_{-i}H^n$ be orthogonal to $E_{i+1}$, where $L\lambda=0$. First we show $\lambda\in W_{-i}H^{n-2}$. Otherwise $\lambda\in W_0$ has a largest graded weight $a$ with $-i<a\le0$ and $[\lambda]_a\ne0$ in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^{n-2}$; since $\alpha=\eta\lambda\in W_{-i}$ and $-i<a$, the graded class $[\alpha]_a=0$, while $[\alpha]_a=\eta[\lambda]_a$ because $\eta$ preserves $W$; as $a\le0$, hypothesis (a) makes $\eta:\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^{n-2}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^n$ injective, a contradiction. Next, centered hard Lefschetz decomposes $\lambda$ along the graded pieces: because $L^i:\operatorname{Gr}^W_i\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}$ is an isomorphism, the $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}$-class of $\lambda$ lifts to a class in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i$ with representative $\lambda_1\in W_iH^{n-2-2i}$, and $\tau_1:=\lambda-L^i\lambda_1\in W_{-i-1}H^{n-2}$. Repeating with $\tau_1$ and $L^{i+1}$, then with the successive remainders and $L^{i+2},L^{i+3},\dots$, and using that $W$ is a finite filtration, we obtain $\lambda=L^i\lambda'$ with $\lambda'\in W_iH^{n-2-2i}$; indeed at stage $t$ the correction $L^{t-1}\lambda_t$ lies in $W_{i-(t-1)}H^{n-2-2i}$, so all corrections lie in $W_i$. Then $L^{i+1}\lambda'=L\lambda=0$. Every class of $\ker(L^{i+1}:\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH^{n-2-2i}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{i-2i-2})$ has an actual lift in $W_iH^{n-2-2i}$ annihilated by $L^{i+1}$: for any lift the error $L^{i+1}\lambda''$ lies in $W_{-i-3}H^n$, and the homogeneous-string description of [F2] shows $L^{i+1}:W_{i-1}H^{n-2-2i}\to W_{-i-3}H^n$ is surjective, since on each string it carries the vector of weight $b+2i+2$ onto the vector of weight $b$ for every weight $b\le-i-3$; subtracting a preimage of the error from $\lambda''$ gives the required lift. Pairing the orthogonality of $\alpha$ to $E_{i+1}$ with these lifts $\beta'$ shows $0=\int_X\alpha\wedge\eta^{i+1}\beta'=\int_X\eta^{i+2}L^i\lambda'\wedge\beta'=q_i([\lambda'],[\beta'])$ for every class $[\beta']$ in $\ker(L^{i+1}:\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH^{n-2-2i}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{i-2i-2})$. Hypothesis (b) now forces $[\lambda']=0$, that is, $\lambda'\in W_{i-1}H^{n-2-2i}$, and since $\eta$ preserves $W$ while $L$ shifts it by $-2$ one gets $\alpha=\eta L^i\lambda'\in W_{-i-1}H^n$. This proves the converse inclusion and completes the induction, so for $i$ beyond the finite filtration, $M\cap E_1^\perp\cap E_2^\perp\cap\cdots=0$.

Let $u_\epsilon\in\Lambda_\epsilon$. Commutation of the two even-degree classes $\eta,L$ gives $\eta^j u_\epsilon=(-\epsilon^{-1})^jL^ju_\epsilon$, hence $\int_Xu_\epsilon\wedge\eta^jz=(-\epsilon^{-1})^j\int_Xu_\epsilon\wedge L^jz=0$ for every $z$ with $L^jz=0$. Passing to the limit, $\Lambda\subseteq E_j^\perp$ for every $j\ge1$. By step 3.1, $\Lambda\cap M=0$. The rank of $L:H^n\to H^{n+2}$ equals the rank of $L:H^{n-2}\to H^n$, because the two maps are adjoint under the Poincaré pairings of [F1]; moreover $\eta:H^{n-2}\to H^n$ is injective by [F1]. Therefore $\dim D=b_n-\operatorname{rk}\bigl(L:H^n\to H^{n+2}\bigr)=\bigl(b_n-b_{n-2}\bigr)+\bigl(b_{n-2}-\operatorname{rk}\bigl(L:H^{n-2}\to H^n\bigr)\bigr)=\dim\Lambda+\dim M$, using $\dim\Lambda=d=b_n-b_{n-2}$ from step 1.1. Since $\Lambda\oplus M\subseteq D$ (both summands lie in $D$: $\Lambda$ by step 1.1 and $M$ because $L\eta=\eta L$ kills $\eta\ker L$) and the dimensions agree, $D=\Lambda\oplus M$; and because $\Lambda\subseteq E_1^\perp$ while $M=E_1$, this sum is orthogonal. Moreover $\Lambda\subseteq D\cap\bigcap_jE_j^\perp$ has dimension $\dim D-\dim M=\dim\Lambda$ and $M\cap\bigcap_jE_j^\perp=0$, so the inclusion is an equality, giving the asserted characterization of $\Lambda$.

Poincaré duality identifies the orthogonal complement of $D$ inside $H^n$ with the image of $L:H^{n-2}\to H^n$, by the adjointness used in step 4.1. On a homogeneous string the kernel of $L$ is the last vector $L^{\ell-1}v$, of weight $1-\ell$; this vector lies in the image of $L$ precisely when $\ell>1$, equivalently when its weight is negative, so $D\cap\operatorname{im}L=D\cap W_{-1}H^n=R$ and by definition $\operatorname{rad}(D)=D\cap D^\perp=D\cap\operatorname{im}L=R$. An orthogonal decomposition of a finite-dimensional space with radical $R$ descends to an orthogonal decomposition of the nondegenerate quotient: if $x=x_\Lambda+x_M\in R$ is paired with each summand separately, orthogonality of the decomposition and $x\in\operatorname{rad}$ show both components are radical, so $R=(R\cap\Lambda)\oplus(R\cap M)$ and the induced form on each quotient summand $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap R)$ and $M/(M\cap R)$ is nondegenerate.

The classical Hermitian form $Q_n(Ca,\bar a)$ of [F1] is positive on every $\Lambda_\epsilon$, because $\Lambda_\epsilon$ is the degree-$n$ primitive space of the Kähler class $L+\epsilon\eta$. For $a\in\Lambda$ choose $a_\epsilon\in\Lambda_\epsilon$ with $a_\epsilon\to a$; by continuity $Q_n(Ca,\bar a)=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}Q_n(Ca_\epsilon,\bar a_\epsilon)\ge0$, so the form is semipositive on $\Lambda$. The Hodge stability of $\Lambda$ and of $R=D\cap W_{-1}$, together with $\eta$- and $L$-stability of $W$, makes $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap R)$ a Hodge quotient. Step 5.1 gives nondegeneracy of the induced form there, and a nondegenerate semipositive Hermitian form is positive definite. The Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations pass from the ambient degree-$n$ cohomology of [F1], so this restriction is a polarization with exactly the sign $\epsilon(n)$ of [F1]. In $D/R$ the orthogonal complement of the image of $M$ is the image of $\Lambda$, since the decomposition of step 5.1 is orthogonal. Every Hodge subspace of that complement inherits the positive definite form, hence is polarized; this proves the final assertion, and in particular the middle double primitive subspace is polarized as soon as its graded primitive condition identifies it with such a Hodge subspace. The degenerate cases (empty or zero graded pieces, $d=0$, and the trivial string of length one with weight $0$) are covered by the same formulas, which then reduce to identities between zero-dimensional spaces.

citations.quote: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be any field. On $D_c^b(X;k)$ for a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, middle perversity is given on smooth complex strata $S$ by the two inequalities $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$. These inequalities define a bounded t structure ([[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]]) on $D_c^b(X;k)$, independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. Verdier duality exchanges its two aisles. The heart is abelian and of finite length, and its simple objects are the intersection complexes $j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems $L$ ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports $Z$. Open restriction is perverse exact. Heart objects have no negative Hom, and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division $k$-algebra. This is the ORDINARY category: no equivariant category, no normalization, no semisimplicity and no noncharacteristic theorem is used or asserted.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].

derivations.claim: Put $Q=j^*P$. The localization triangle $i_*i^!P\to P\to Rj_*Q\to$ has both outer terms $i_*i^!P$ and $Rj_*Q$ in the lower perverse aisle: $i^!$ preserves it, $i_*$ is perverse exact and $Rj_*$ preserves it by [F1]. Its perverse cohomology exact sequence therefore begins $0\to{}^pH^0(i_*i^!P)\to{}^pH^0P$, and ${}^pH^0(i_*i^!P)=i_*A$ because $i_*$ is perverse exact; so the degree-zero adjunction map is a monomorphism $a:i_*A\rightarrowtail P$. Dually, the triangle $Rj_!Q\to P\to i_*i^*P\to$ has its outer terms in the upper perverse aisle, so its perverse cohomology sequence ends with ${}^pH^0P\to{}^pH^0(i_*i^*P)\to0$, that is, the adjunction map $b:P\twoheadrightarrow i_*B$ is an epimorphism. Full faithfulness of $i_*$ identifies the composite $ba:i_*A\to i_*B$ with $i_*\alpha$ for the induced map $\alpha:A\to B$.

A morphism $i_*T\to P$ from a supported perverse sheaf corresponds by adjunction to $T\to i^!P$. Since $i^!P\in{}^pD^{\ge0}$, its truncation triangle is $A\to i^!P\to C\to A[1]$, with $C={}^p\tau_{\ge1}i^!P$. Orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(T,C)=0=\operatorname{Hom}(T,C[-1])$, because $C\in{}^pD^{\ge1}$ and $C[-1]\in{}^pD^{\ge2}$. The Hom exact sequence therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(T,A)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^!P)$, so every supported morphism into $P$ factors uniquely through $a$. Thus $i_*A$ is the largest supported subobject. Dually, the truncation of $i^*P\in{}^pD^{\le0}$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(B,T)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(i^*P,T)$, so every supported quotient factors uniquely through $b$, and $i_*B$ is the largest supported quotient.

Suppose $\alpha$ is invertible, and define $r=(i_*\alpha)^{-1}b:P\to i_*A$. Then $ra=(i_*\alpha)^{-1}ba=1_{i_*A}$. As $a$ is a monomorphism and $r$ a retraction in the abelian heart, $P=i_*A\oplus C$ with $C=\ker r$, and $j^*C=Q$ because $j^*$ is exact, $j^*i_*A=0$ and $j^*P=Q$. A subobject $S\subseteq C$ supported on $Z$ is also a supported subobject of $P$, so by step 2.1 its inclusion into $P$ factors through $a$; applying $r$ makes that factorization zero, while $S\subseteq\ker r$, so $S=0$. A supported quotient $C\twoheadrightarrow i_*T$ composed with the projection $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ is a morphism $P\to i_*T$; by step 2.1 it factors as $h\,b$ with $h:i_*B\to i_*T$, and it kills $i_*A$, so $0=h\,ba=h\,i_*\alpha$ and $h=0$; since $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ is an epimorphism, the quotient map $C\to i_*T$ is zero. Thus $C$ has no nonzero supported subobject and no nonzero supported quotient.

Let $C$ be a perverse extension of $Q$ with no nonzero supported subobject or quotient. The counit of $Rj_!\dashv j^*$ and the unit of $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ induce $f:{}^pH^0Rj_!Q\to C$ and $g:C\to{}^pH^0Rj_*Q$. Their restrictions to $U$ are identities, so the cokernel of $f$ and the kernel of $g$ are supported on $Z$ and must vanish. Thus $f$ is epic and $g$ is monic. Their composite is the natural comparison: by the heart adjunction of [F1], a morphism ${}^pH^0Rj_!Q\to{}^pH^0Rj_*Q$ is determined by its restriction $Q\to Q$, which here is the identity. Consequently $C\simeq\operatorname{im}(gf)=j_{!*}Q$. By [F1], this intermediate extension itself has neither supported subobjects nor supported quotients.

Suppose $P\simeq i_*T\oplus j_{!*}Q$ for a perverse $T$ on $Z$. By step 4.1, $j_{!*}Q$ has no nonzero subobject or quotient supported on $Z$, so ${}^pH^0i^!j_{!*}Q=0={}^pH^0i^*j_{!*}Q$; and $i^!i_*=1=i^*i_*$ exhibits $A=B=T$ on the $i_*T$ summand, with the adjunction maps the identities. Additivity of the exact functors $i^!$, $i^*$ on the displayed direct sum therefore identifies $A=B=T$ and $\alpha=1_T$, an isomorphism. Combined with steps 3.1 and 4.1 this proves the equivalence: $\alpha$ is invertible if and only if $P\simeq i_*A\oplus j_{!*}j^*P$. For $Z=\{y\}$ the perverse heart on the point consists of finite-dimensional vector spaces in degree zero by [F1], so $A=H^0(i_y^!P)$ and $B=H^0(i_y^*P)$ are finite vector spaces and the criterion reduces to invertibility of the costalk-to-stalk map. Nothing in the argument asserts invertibility of $\alpha$ for projective direct images; that is the separate intersection-form obligation.

Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced quasi-projective complex
algebraic varieties, and prescribe finitely many closed or locally closed
algebraic subsets in source and target. There exist finite smooth complex
algebraic Whitney (a),(b) stratifications with frontier on $X$ and $Y$
respecting all prescribed subsets, such that each source stratum maps
surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. A further finite algebraic
stratification may be prescribed and refined. The analytic strata are smooth
complex manifolds and the restrictions are smooth submersions. If $f$ is proper
in the analytic topology, in particular if it is a projective algebraic
morphism, the whole restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ over any target stratum is
proper; no restriction of $f$ to a nonclosed individual source stratum is
asserted proper.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $P$ be a bounded algebraically constructible complex on a complex variety $Y$. If $a:X\to Y$ is smooth of pure relative complex dimension $d$, then $a^*[d]$ is perverse-exact and $a^!=a^*[2d]$ in complex orientation. Fix a finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification $\mathfrak S$ of $Y$. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is the restriction of a smooth complex closed embedding of codimension $c$ transverse to every stratum of $\mathfrak S$, then $i^*[-c]$ is perverse-exact on the subcategory of bounded complexes whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant of finite rank on every stratum of $\mathfrak S$, and $i^!P\cong i^*P[-2c]$ for every $P$ in this subcategory. No assertion is made for arbitrary closed embeddings.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. For an affine morphism $u:X\to Y$ of complex algebraic varieties and finite-dimensional field coefficients, $Ru_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ and $Ru_!$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Y)$. More precisely a bounded constructible $K$ belongs to ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ if and only if $H^q(V,K)=0$ for every affine Zariski open $V\subset Y$ and every $q>0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction. If $Z$ is a complex affine algebraic variety of complex dimension $d$ and $F$ is an algebraically constructible sheaf of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, then $H^q(Z,F)=0$ for $q>d$. More precisely the bound is the dimension of the closure of its support. If $P\in{}^pD^{\le0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q>0$. If $P\in{}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H_c^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q<0$. The empty variety and zero coefficients give zero groups.

Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective map of complex varieties, with a fixed closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ and $d\ge1$. Set $Y'=Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p':X'\to X$, and let $i:\mathcal X\hookrightarrow X'$ be the universal hyperplane incidence. Write $g=(f\times1)i$, and for $K\in\operatorname{Perv}(X;k)$ put $M=i^*p'^*K[d-1]$. Then $M$ is perverse and the restriction/Gysin maps give isomorphisms $p^*{}^pH^l(Rf_*K)[d]\to{}^pH^{l+1}(Rg_*M)$ for $l\le-2$ and monomorphisms for $l=-1$, with dual isomorphisms for $l\ge2$ and epimorphisms for $l=1$. In particular $p^*{}^pH^{-1}(Rf_*K)[d]$ identifies with the largest perverse subobject of ${}^pH^0(Rg_*M)$ belonging to the essential image of $p^*[d]$, and $p^*{}^pH^1(Rf_*K)[d]$ with the largest such quotient.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties with $X$ smooth, nonempty and irreducible of dimension $n$. Fix a projective embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ with $d\ge1$ and let $Y_i=\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}$. Put $r(f)=\max_{Y_i\ne\varnothing}(2i+\dim Y_i-n)$. For the universal hyperplane incidence $g:\mathcal X\to Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ one has $r(g)\le r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$. If $r(f)=0$, $g$ is small: it has defect zero and every positive-fiber-dimensional stratum gives a strictly negative defect contribution.

There is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the hyperplane parameter space such that every hyperplane $H$ in it has smooth $X_H=X\cap H$ and satisfies the same conclusions for $f_H:X_H\to Y$: its defect is at most $r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$, and it is small if $r(f)=0$. Empty hyperplane sections are omitted from the defect computation and have zero pushforward. Successive general sections therefore lower a positive defect at every nonempty step. A finite prescribed algebraic Whitney stratification can also be met transversally by shrinking this open subset when the separately supplied stratified transversality theorem is applicable.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field of characteristic $0$, let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible classical
varieties over $k$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and let
$f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of classical varieties. Assume $X$ is smooth
over $k$, that is, the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth
in the locally-standard-smooth sense of [[def-smooth-morphism-classical]]
(equivalently, since $k$ is perfect, $X$ is regular). Then:

1. there is a dense open subvariety $U\subseteq Y$ such that the restriction
   $$f^{-1}(U)\longrightarrow U$$
   is a smooth morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes; when $f$ is not dominant
   one may take $U$ with $f^{-1}(U)=\varnothing$, the empty morphism being
   smooth;
2. if in addition $f$ is dominant, there is a nonempty open (hence dense)
   $V\subseteq U$ such that for every closed point $y\in V$ the
   scheme-theoretic fibre
   $$X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k(y)$$
   ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]]) is nonempty, smooth over $k$, and of pure
   dimension $r=\dim X-\dim Y$.

Neither $Y$ nor $f$ is required to be smooth or flat, the fibres are not
required to be irreducible or connected, and no statement is made about the
size of $U$ or $V$. The characteristic-$0$ hypothesis enters through the
critical-locus dimension bound of
[[lem-critical-locus-image-dimension-bound]] in claim 1 and through the
perfectness of $k$; the failure of the target-open statement for a
non-smooth source and the positive-characteristic failure of the
corresponding source-side statement are recorded on the counterexample page of
this pair.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be an
algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. Let $X$ be a smooth
$k$-scheme of finite type that admits a locally closed immersion into some
projective space over $k$ (that is, $X$ is smooth and quasi-projective;
[[def-locally-closed-immersion]]), let $L$ be an invertible
$\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $W\subseteq\Gamma(X,L)$ be a nonzero
finite-dimensional linear system, with $\dim_kW=r+1$, base locus
$\operatorname{Bs}(W)$ and $X^\circ=X\smallsetminus\operatorname{Bs}(W)$
([[def-linear-system-base-locus]]); thus $\mathbf P(W)=\mathbf P^r_k$.

Then there is a nonempty Zariski-open subset $U\subseteq\mathbf P(W)$ such
that for every closed point $[s]\in U$ of the $k$-scheme $\mathbf P(W)$
(equivalently, by
[[thm-classical-varieties-equivalent-integral-separated-finite-type-schemes]],
every classical parameter $[s]$ lying in $U$), and every representative
$0\ne s\in W$, the closed subscheme $Z(s)\cap X^\circ\subseteq X^\circ$ is
smooth over $k$. Thus the property "the member $Z(s)\cap X^\circ$ is smooth
over $k$" holds for general members of $W$ in the sense of
[[def-linear-system-base-locus]], with generalizing open set $U$; the members
are closed subschemes of the open subscheme $X^\circ$, which may be empty, and
$U$ contains classical parameters.

In particular, suppose $X\ne\varnothing$, fix a locally closed immersion
$X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$, let $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ be the hyperplane line
bundle of that immersion, and let $W_h\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$ be
the hyperplane system, the span of the restrictions of the degree-one forms
([[def-linear-system-base-locus]]). Then $\operatorname{Bs}(W_h)=\varnothing$,
and there is a nonempty Zariski-open subset $U\subseteq\mathbf P(W_h)$ such
that for every closed point $[s]\in U$ the scheme-theoretic hyperplane section
$X\times_{\mathbf P^N_k}V_+(F)$ of $X$ — for any degree-one form $F$ with
$F|_X=s$, equivalently the zero scheme $Z(s)$
([[lem-zero-scheme-of-line-bundle-section]]) — is smooth over $k$.

No irreducibility or connectedness of $X$ or of the members is asserted, and
no statement is made about the dimension or the nonemptiness of the members.

Let $X\subseteq\mathbf P_k^N$ be irreducible of dimension $d\ge1$. If $f$ is homogeneous of positive degree and does not vanish identically on $X$, then $X\cap V_+(f)$ is nonempty and every irreducible component has dimension $d-1$.

Work over a fixed algebraically closed field $k$, with the Axiom of Choice. Classical varieties are separated and admit finite affine covers; they may be reducible or empty unless irreducibility is specified. Irreducible means nonempty. All fibres and points below are classical closed-point fibres and points.

Assume AC. Let $E\to M$ be a smooth $R$-oriented rank-$r$ numerable real vector bundle in the scope of the Thom theorem over a closed $R$-oriented smooth $n$-manifold $M$, let $s:M\to E$ be a smooth section transverse to the zero section with zero locus $Z=s^{-1}(0)$ carrying the induced orientation of [[lem-normal-bundle-of-the-zero-locus-of-a-transverse-section]], and let $u_E$ be the normalized Thom class of $E$. Choose a smooth bundle metric by [[thm-every-smooth-vector-bundle-admits-a-smooth-bundle-metric]]. Lift $u_E$ uniquely to $\widetilde u_E\in H^r(D(E),D(E)\setminus s_0(M);R)$: restriction to $(D(E),S(E))$ is an isomorphism because the punctured fibres retract radially onto their spheres. After composing $s$ with the fibre-radial diffeomorphism $v\mapsto v/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}$ onto the open unit disc bundle (which fixes $Z$ and has derivative the identity at every zero), the pair pullback $s^*(\widetilde u_E)\in H^r(M,M\setminus Z;R)$ is defined, and it equals the image of the normal Thom class $u_{\nu_Z}$ under the tubular excision isomorphism supplied by [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]] and [[thm-excision-for-singular-cohomology]]. Consequently its image in $H^r(M;R)$ is the Euler class $e(E)$ of [[def-euler-class-by-zero-section-pullback-of-the-thom-class]]: the relative pullback of the Thom class along any transverse section computes $e(E)$. The zero section defines $e(E)$ by its absolute pullback; over a nonempty base it is transverse to itself exactly in rank zero; over an empty base transversality is vacuous.

Assume AC. Let $L,M$ be numerable complex line bundles over a path-connected
CW complex with a vertex basepoint, or over a path-connected paracompact
Hausdorff CGWH space of CW homotopy type. Then
$$c_1(L\otimes M)=c_1(L)+c_1(M),\qquad c_1(L^*)=-c_1(L),\qquad c_1(\overline L)=-c_1(L),$$
where $L^*$ is the dual line and $\overline L$ the conjugate line.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
suppliers below. For a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of pure dimension
$n$ with a chosen ample line class $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, its rational
cohomology is finite-dimensional pure Hodge in each degree, functorial for
pullback along holomorphic maps of the analytifications. Cup product has Hodge
type $(0,0)$ and $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$. For $0\le k\le n$ the
hard-Lefschetz maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are rational isomorphisms,
and for $k>n$ so are the complementary maps $\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$; the rational
primitive summands satisfy the Hodge–Riemann positivity of
[[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], and
the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization. Rational
Hodge substructures split orthogonally. The same absolute positivity and
hard-Lefschetz statements hold for real Kähler classes, and primitive kernels
vary continuously along Kähler families. Rational splittings and isomorphisms
persist after extension to any characteristic-zero field. This package does
not supply weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular
intersection-cohomology purity, or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with a bounded t-structure, with truncation functors and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]. Let $K\in\mathcal T$ and let $L:K\to K[2]$ be a morphism such that for every integer $j\ge0$ the map
$$H^{-j}_t(L^j):H^{-j}_t(K)\longrightarrow H^{-j}_t(K[2j])\cong H^j_t(K)$$
is an isomorphism, where $L^j:=L[2j-2]\circ\cdots\circ L[2]\circ L$ is the $j$-fold iterate (so $L^0=1_K$) and the identification is the shift isomorphism $H^j_t(K)\cong H^{-j}_t(K[2j])$ of that lemma. Then there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong\bigoplus_j H^j_t(K)[-j]$$
in $\mathcal T$; the sum is finite because the t-structure is bounded. The isomorphism is not asserted to be canonical, and no compatibility with primitive lifts is claimed: this is the abstract splitting criterion, not the stronger primitive-compatible decomposition used in the Hodge theory of projective maps. The degenerate case in which $H^{-n}_t(K)$ and $H^n_t(K)$ are both zero (they vanish together because $H^{-n}_t(L^n)$ is an isomorphism) is covered by the same formulas, all of which are then the zero maps between zero objects.

Let $H^j$, $j\in\mathbb Z$, be objects of an abelian category, zero for all but finitely many $j$, and let $L_j:H^j\to H^{j+2}$ be morphisms whose iterates give isomorphisms $L^r:H^{-r}\to H^r$ for every $r\ge0$, with $L^0=1_{H^0}$. Put $P^{-r}:=\ker\bigl(L^{r+1}:H^{-r}\to H^{r+2}\bigr)$ for $r\ge0$, and $P^{-r}=0$ for $r<0$. Then for every $r\ge0$ the powers of $L$ induce finite direct sum decompositions
$$H^{-r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^jP^{-r-2j},\qquad H^{r}=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}L^{r+j}P^{-r-2j},$$
where $L^jP^{-r-2j}$ denotes the image of the restriction of $L^j$ to the subobject $P^{-r-2j}\subseteq H^{-r-2j}$, and likewise for $L^{r+j}P^{-r-2j}$. Each displayed power $L^j$ or $L^{r+j}$ restricts to a monomorphism on its primitive source, and both decompositions are natural for morphisms commuting with $L$. This is a decomposition statement for graded objects in an abelian category; it does not identify primitive objects with classes annihilated by an untruncated map on a derived splitting of a complex.

Let $N$ be a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space $H$ over a field $F$ ([[def-nilpotent-endomorphism]]). An **admissible filtration** is an increasing finite filtration $W$ of $H$ by linear subspaces ([[def-linear-subspace]]): $W_i\subseteq W_{i+1}$ for all $i$, $W_i=0$ for all sufficiently negative $i$, $W_i=H$ for all sufficiently positive $i$, such that

$$N(W_i)\subseteq W_{i-2}\quad\text{for all }i,\qquad N^r:\operatorname{Gr}^W_r\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-r}\text{ is an isomorphism for every }r\ge0,$$

where $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i:=W_i/W_{i-1}$ and the second map is the one induced by $N^r$, which is well defined because $N^r(W_r)\subseteq W_{-r}$ and $N^r(W_{r-1})\subseteq W_{-r-1}$. There is a unique admissible filtration $W$, and it is given intrinsically by

$$W_i=\sum_{a,b\ge0,\ a-b=i}\ker N^{a+1}\cap\operatorname{im}N^b .$$

If in addition $S$ is a nondegenerate bilinear form on $H$ with $S(Nv,w)+S(v,Nw)=0$ for all $v,w$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]], [[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]), and $U^\perp:=\{x\in H:S(u,x)=0\text{ for every }u\in U\}$ for a subspace $U$, then $(W_i)^\perp=W_{-i-1}$ for every $i$, and consequently $S$ induces a perfect pairing between $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-i}$; moreover for $i\ge0$ the form $S_i([v],[w]):=S(v,N^iw)$ on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_i$ is well defined and nondegenerate.

Assume AC, let $X$ be smooth projective of complex dimension $n$, and write $H^m=H^m(X;\mathbb R)$. Let $\eta$ be a Kähler class, and let $L$ be a real $(1,1)$ class such that $L+\epsilon\eta$ is Kähler for every $\epsilon>0$. Use the centered nilpotent filtration $W$ of cup product by $L$ on total cohomology, with $L:W_a\to W_{a-2}$ and $L^a:\operatorname{Gr}^W_a\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-a}$ an isomorphism. Assume the following three precise hypotheses, to be furnished by the preceding stages of a projective induction:

(a) $W$ is a Hodge filtration by subspaces stable under $\eta$, and $\eta:\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^{n-2}\to\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH^n$ is injective for every $a\le0$.

(b) For every $i\ge0$, the form
$$q_i(x,y)=\int_X\eta^{i+2}L^i x\wedge y$$
on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_iH^{n-2-2i}$ restricts nondegenerately to the kernel of $L^{i+1}$ there. This includes well-definedness of that induced form; it concerns only nonmiddle graded primitive forms.

(c) Poincaré pairing between complementary ordinary degrees annihilates $W_a\times W_b$ when $a+b<0$.

Set $D=\ker(L:H^n\to H^{n+2})$, $R=D\cap W_{-1}H^n$, and $M=\eta\ker(L:H^{n-2}\to H^n)$. Then the limit $\Lambda=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\ker(L+\epsilon\eta:H^n\to H^{n+2})$ exists as a Hodge subspace, and
$$\Lambda=D\cap\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigl(\eta^j\ker(L^j:H^{n-2j}\to H^n)\bigr)^\perp,\qquad D=\Lambda\mathbin{\perp\oplus}M.$$
The radical of the Poincaré form on $D$ is exactly $R$. Its restriction, with the classical degree-$n$ Hodge sign, polarizes $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap R)$. Consequently it polarizes every Hodge subspace of $D/R$ orthogonal to the image of $M$. In particular this applies to the middle double primitive subspace once that subspace's graded primitive condition identifies it with such a Hodge subspace. No polarization or semisimplicity in the middle is assumed in (a)–(c).

Assume AC as inherited from the ordinary constructible suppliers, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed complex algebraic inclusion with complementary open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$. Let $P$ be an ordinary constructible perverse sheaf over a characteristic-zero field. Set $A={}^pH^0i^!P$ and $B={}^pH^0i^*P$. The adjunction maps define a natural morphism $\alpha:A\to B$. It is an isomorphism if and only if
$$P\simeq i_*A\oplus j_{!*}j^*P.$$
More precisely, $i_*A$ is the largest subobject of $P$ supported on $Z$, $i_*B$ is its largest quotient supported there, and their composite equals $i_*\alpha$. If $\alpha$ is invertible, these canonical maps give the displayed splitting. For $Z=\{y\}$, $A=H^0(i_y^!P)$ and $B=H^0(i_y^*P)$ are finite vector spaces, so the criterion is exactly invertibility of the degree-zero costalk-to-stalk map. This criterion does not assert that that map is invertible for projective direct images.

Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any smooth projective compactification, and let
$g:Y\to U$ be a morphism with $Y$ proper (possibly singular and reducible).
Then, in every degree $n$,
$$\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{(jg)^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q))=\operatorname{im}(H^n(U,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{g^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)).$$
Both images are pure Hodge substructures of weight $n$. This includes the
restriction of a smooth projective total space to a proper singular fiber through
an open subvariety, which is the exact use in de Cataldo-Migliorini
Proposition 8.3.2 of arXiv:math/0306030v1 (pp. 64-65).

Assume AC. The rational cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ of every proper complex
algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]) with weights at most $n$. For a
morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper and $U$ smooth quasiprojective, its pullback
$H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on
$U$. If $Y\to X$ is proper with $X$ smooth projective of pure dimension $d$, the
proper homological class map
$$H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$$
is a mixed Hodge morphism after the indicated Tate twist. Its image, and
consequently the untwisted image in $H^{2d-i}(X)$, is a pure Hodge substructure.
No smoothness of $Y$ is assumed. For an ambient $X$ with components of
different dimensions, the class map is the direct sum of these maps on
$Y\times_X X_c\to X_c$, using each component dimension $d_c$ separately.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $f:X\to S$ is smooth projective with
$S$ a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety, then every local system
$R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is
semisimple over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]) and remains semisimple
after scalar extension to every characteristic-zero field. More generally the
complex local system of every geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation is
semisimple. The algebraic realization and geometric integral lattice are
essential hypotheses; no claim is made for every polarized analytic variation
on a punctured disk.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $U$ is a nonempty
Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety $S$, then
$U$ is path connected and $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ is surjective for every
$s\in U$ ([[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]]).

derivations.claim: The pair $(r,m)$ consists of nonnegative integers: on a generic fibre of dimension $a=n-m$, its defect contribution is $2a+m-n=a\ge0$, and there are finitely many algebraic fibre-dimension loci. If $m=0$, the map factors through a point. Relative $\eta$ hard Lefschetz is absolute hard Lefschetz, the finite point-derived category splits by ordinary truncations, all point local systems are semisimple, graded $L$ hard Lefschetz is zero-to-zero away from its centre, and double primitive positivity is absolute Hodge–Riemann. This proves the base without an unstated relative theorem. For positive image dimension use the lower package only on the strictly lower maps specified in the following constructions.

Construction A gives the actual divisor identity: smooth codimension-one purity has the positive normal disk counit, transverse section Thom comparison identifies its restriction–trace composite with its line class, and the universal evaluation line is the source line tensored with the parameter $\mathcal O(1)$. The exact shifts are $R:A_0\to C_0[1]$ and $G:C_0\to A_0[1]$. Tensor naturality with ${}^p\tau_{\le j}$ makes the degree-two target parameter class act by zero on perverse degree $j\to j+2$. Thus the composite with $\eta'^{r-1}$ is exactly $\eta^r$ on the required perverse groups. Construction B derives actual general parameter transversality and the fixed target weak-Lefschetz bounds, including basepointfree source smoothness.

Construction C proves relative hard Lefschetz when $r>0$: the universal map has smaller defect, its class $\eta'+h$ is absolutely very ample and induces the same relative operator, and its middle perverse object is semisimple by lower induction. The maximal pullback quotient forbids a kernel in $P_{-1}\xrightarrow{\eta}P_1$; duality supplies surjectivity. Higher powers use outside weak-Lefschetz isomorphisms. For $r=0$, the fibre-dimension support bound and self-duality make $K$ perverse, so the assertion is tautological. The abstract bounded-t splitting gives the finite normalized decomposition. Nonzero perverse degrees are split subquotients of lower-defect universal objects; ordinary heart full faithfulness descends their projectors and duality treats positive degrees, including the complexified local-system clause.

Construction D first proves graded $L$ hard Lefschetz outside perverse degree zero using fixed source cuts, only while their defect is positive. All target cup operators commute with the heart projectors. In degree zero, target-cut restriction/Gysin isomorphisms prove powers at least two. For the first power, strict block-diagonal $L$ action lifts a kernel to an ordinary $L$-kernel; each of its classical Hodge types stays there, without assuming the original perverse filtration Hodge. A nonzero type restricts to a nonzero lower-map middle primitive with positive Hodge–Riemann norm, while the target Thom cup formula makes its integral zero. This contradiction proves injectivity; duality gives an isomorphism. Every chosen source or target map is strictly lower by Construction B.

The intrinsic centered nilpotent filtration now identifies the perverse filtration degree by degree, so its kernel/image formula proves it Hodge. Construction D then restricts nonmiddle double primitives to lower source/target slices, checks their actual graded primitive kernels using the Gysin isomorphisms, and identifies their forms by the Thom cup formula. Lower Hodge–Riemann makes these forms polarizations. The large target-index boundary is zero by cutting to a finite-point image and negative hypercohomology there. Construction E verifies every explicit hypothesis (a)–(c) of the middle limiting lemma, its total pairing symmetry, primitive lifts and the actual middle subspace identification. That lemma gives the remaining $(0,0)$ positivity. This order uses only previously proved nonmiddle forms in the endpoint-limit argument. Construction E explicitly establishes the Kahler hypothesis and derives the finite double primitive decomposition, raw-form orthogonality and transported primitive signs.

Construction F identifies the zero-stratum costalk/stalk map with the graded refined intersection form. Artin on an affine target open gives the graded restriction edge; the actual mixed-Hodge image equality upgrades it to global surjectivity using strictness from the earlier finite normalized splitting. Proper trace duality gives an injective class map. The proper mixed-Hodge class supplier makes its image a pure sub-Hodge structure in $\ker L$. Naturality for genuine perverse $\eta$ projectors decomposes that image into the orthogonal primitive blocks, and each block's sign-adjusted polarization restricts nondegenerately. Therefore the actual intersection matrix is invertible, without current middle semisimplicity or a global primitive-compatible lift.

Construction G constructs projective target slices through an arbitrary positive-dimensional stratum point: the constrained system is smooth away from its fibre base locus by Bertini, and independent differentials along the smooth source stratum maps give smoothness at every point of that fibre. The slices have no larger defect and smaller image dimension. Their normalized extraordinary/ordinary compositions reflect the actual local costalk/stalk map with both real normal shifts $-2s$ cancelled. Lower slice intersection invertibility gives the isomorphism along every such stratum. The formal closed-support criterion then inducts over the finite closed-stratum frontier and yields an IC decomposition of $P_0$ before local-system semisimplicity is used.

Construction H gives the actual smooth projective moving family and its quotient onto each intermediate-dimensional stratum system. Its good algebraic section is constructed by a rational point in an explicit product-projective generic fibre; dominance is not mistaken for a section. Smooth incidence parameter maps and the graph factorization have net perverse shift $(d-s)+s-d=0$. The fibre stalk map is the lower-map global graded restriction, hence surjective. Independent Gauss–Manin semisimplicity and dense-open fundamental-group surjectivity imply both rational and complexified semisimplicity. Construction G supplies the explicit top-stratum identification with $R^{n-m}f_*\mathbb Q$, and point strata are finite vector spaces. Applying intermediate extension to these finite decompositions makes every IC summand a finite sum of simple IC objects.

Steps 3.1–8.1 prove every clause of the package in the Statement under exactly its lower-package hypothesis. Every source slice, universal family or target slice used has a smaller nonnegative lexicographic pair, and step 1.1 supplies the image-zero base; thus this lemma is the actual simultaneous induction step. The projective constructions preserve arbitrary fibre dimensions and singular proper fibres. All sums, projector decompositions and cohomological models are finite. No finite-ADE restriction, arithmetic purity or fibre affine-paving hypothesis entered.

risk_review.notes: Reviewed all nine main steps, full constructions A-H, every declared supplier Statement, and the relevant ordinary six-operation/recollement, universal-hyperplane and Hodge-substructure proofs. A fixes the positive Thom counit and all R/G shifts; target tensor naturality kills the parameter perverse-degree action. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, with $X$ smooth connected of dimension $n$, let $\eta$ be a very ample source class, and put $L=f^*c_1(B)$ for a very ample target line $B$. Write $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, $P_b={}^pH^bK$, $F_bH^q(X)=\operatorname{im}(H^{q-n}(Y,{}^p\tau_{\le b}K)\to H^q(X))$, $H_b^q=F_bH^q/F_{b-1}H^q$, $m=\dim f(X)$ and

$$r(f)=\max_i\bigl(2i+\dim\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}-n\bigr).$$

Consider the following package: relative $\eta$ hard Lefschetz $\eta^i:P_{-i}\simeq P_i$; a finite normalized splitting $K\simeq\bigoplus_bP_b[-b]$; semisimplicity of every $P_b$ with semisimple complexifications of its IC local systems; target graded hard Lefschetz $L^j:H_b^{n+b-j}\simeq H_b^{n+b+j}$; pure Hodge structures of their ordinary degree on the canonical graded groups; and polarized orthogonal double primitive decomposition. The double primitive space is

$$\mathcal P_{-i}^{-j}=\ker\eta^{i+1}\cap\ker L^{j+1}\subset H_{-i}^{n-i-j},\qquad i,j\ge0,$$

with polarization $Q_t(u,v)=(-1)^{t(t-1)/2}\int_X\eta^iL^ju\wedge v$, $t=n-i-j$, and positivity $Q_t(Cu,\bar u)>0$ for nonzero $u$, where $C$ acts on type $(p,q)$ by $i^{p-q}$. Filtration and primitive forms are the canonical graded ones; no primitive-compatible lift to ordinary global cohomology is assumed.

If this package holds for all smooth connected projective-source maps of lexicographically smaller pair $(r,m)$, with $r$ primary, then it holds for $f$. The image-dimension-zero base is supplied by absolute polarized Hodge theory and finite linear algebra. Finite disconnected smooth sources are handled componentwise. The statement preserves arbitrary projective fibres and requires neither semismallness nor affine paving.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
suppliers below. For a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of pure dimension
$n$ with a chosen ample line class $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, its rational
cohomology is finite-dimensional pure Hodge in each degree, functorial for
pullback along holomorphic maps of the analytifications. Cup product has Hodge
type $(0,0)$ and $\ell$ has type $(1,1)$. For $0\le k\le n$ the
hard-Lefschetz maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are rational isomorphisms,
and for $k>n$ so are the complementary maps $\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$; the rational
primitive summands satisfy the Hodge–Riemann positivity of
[[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], and
the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization. Rational
Hodge substructures split orthogonally. The same absolute positivity and
hard-Lefschetz statements hold for real Kähler classes, and primitive kernels
vary continuously along Kähler families. Rational splittings and isomorphisms
persist after extension to any characteristic-zero field. This package does
not supply weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular
intersection-cohomology purity, or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with a bounded t-structure, with truncation functors and t-cohomology as in [[def-truncation-functors-and-cohomology-of-a-t-structure]] and [[lem-t-cohomology-is-additive-shift-compatible-and-detects-amplitude]]. Let $K\in\mathcal T$ and let $L:K\to K[2]$ be a morphism such that for every integer $j\ge0$ the map
$$H^{-j}_t(L^j):H^{-j}_t(K)\longrightarrow H^{-j}_t(K[2j])\cong H^j_t(K)$$
is an isomorphism, where $L^j:=L[2j-2]\circ\cdots\circ L[2]\circ L$ is the $j$-fold iterate (so $L^0=1_K$) and the identification is the shift isomorphism $H^j_t(K)\cong H^{-j}_t(K[2j])$ of that lemma. Then there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong\bigoplus_j H^j_t(K)[-j]$$
in $\mathcal T$; the sum is finite because the t-structure is bounded. The isomorphism is not asserted to be canonical, and no compatibility with primitive lifts is claimed: this is the abstract splitting criterion, not the stronger primitive-compatible decomposition used in the Hodge theory of projective maps. The degenerate case in which $H^{-n}_t(K)$ and $H^n_t(K)$ are both zero (they vanish together because $H^{-n}_t(L^n)$ is an isomorphism) is covered by the same formulas, all of which are then the zero maps between zero objects.

derivations.claim: It suffices to treat a connected component of $X$: the connected components of the smooth variety $X$ are open and closed and there are finitely many of them, and the direct image of their direct sum is the direct sum of the direct images by [F3]. Such a component is irreducible. Replace $Y$ by the projective image of the component with reduced structure; a closed immersion is perverse exact by [F3], so extending by closed support later preserves the splitting and the IC description. For the reduced image the pair $(r,m)=(r(f),\dim f(X))$ consists of nonnegative integers, as in the induction-step supplier [F1]. If $m=0$, the map factors through a point, and [F2] proves the entire asserted package directly, including the semisimplicity of the complexified local systems (which are finite-dimensional vector spaces on a point). The empty source gives the zero complex and is covered by the same statement. For a remaining map fix its pair and assume the package of [F1] for every lexicographically smaller pair.

The exact induction step [F1] now gives the package for the fixed map. The hypothesis of [F1] is the induction hypothesis recorded in step 1.1, and lexicographic order on pairs of nonnegative integers is well-founded, so with the image-dimension-zero base case the package holds for every smooth connected projective-source map. The clauses asserted in the Statement are the relative hard Lefschetz isomorphisms, the finite splitting and the IC description with semisimplicity of the complexified local systems, all of which are clauses of that package. It remains to replace the very ample class used by [F1] by the given ample class $\eta$: by [[thm-ample-powers-very-ample-proper-base]] a sufficiently high power of the given ample bundle is very ample, and if its class is $\eta_0=m\eta$ then the relative hard Lefschetz isomorphisms for $\eta_0$ scale to those for $\eta$ because $\eta^i=m^{-i}\eta_0^i$; the splitting, the IC description and semisimplicity are independent of the chosen ample class.
